postings.conferenceSeries: 47th IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
postings.conferenceText: The IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy is a premier forum for research in computer security and electronic privacy. Since 1980, the conference has brought together researchers and practitioners from academia, industry, and government to present foundational advances as well as impactful applied work. The 2026 edition will take place in San Francisco and covers a broad range of technical, human-centered, and systems-oriented security and privacy research. Applied cryptography; authentication; blockchains and distributed ledgers; cloud security; cyber-physical systems; distributed systems security; economics of security and privacy; embedded and hardware security; formal methods; human-centered security and privacy; intrusion detection; machine-learning security and privacy; malware; network security; operating systems and systems security; privacy-enhancing technologies; program analysis; protocol security; security metrics, policies, and architectures; supply-chain security; web, wireless, and mobile security.

postings.conferenceName: Selected Areas in Cryptography 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: Selected Areas in Cryptography
postings.conferenceText: Selected Areas in Cryptography (SAC 2026) is Canada’s long-running research conference on cryptography and has been held annually since 1994. The conference provides a focused forum for current results in cryptographic theory, algorithms, implementations, and applications, while also highlighting selected special themes. The 2026 edition will be hosted by the University of Ottawa and continues SAC’s role as a specialized venue for both foundational and applied cryptography research. Symmetric-key primitives and designs; cryptographic algorithms and efficient implementations; mathematical and algorithmic aspects of applied cryptology; post-quantum cryptography, including lattice-based and code-based cryptography; implementation, optimization, and analysis techniques for modern cryptosystems.

postings.conferenceName: 31st ACM Symposium on Access Control Models and Technologies 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 31st ACM Symposium on Access Control Models and Technologies
postings.conferenceText: SACMAT 2026 is the 31st ACM Symposium on Access Control Models and Technologies, a specialized venue devoted to the foundations, design, and implementation of access control. The symposium covers theoretical models as well as practical mechanisms for modern distributed, networked, cloud, and data-centric environments. By bringing together researchers and practitioners, SACMAT continues to serve as a core forum for policy specification, enforcement, analysis, and evaluation of secure authorization systems. Access control models and policy languages; authorization logics; attribute-based and relationship-based access control; trust management; identity and federated authorization; access control for cloud, web, mobile, IoT, and distributed systems; privacy-aware access control; policy analysis, verification, and mining; implementation, enforcement, usability, and real-world deployment of access control technologies.

postings.conferenceName: 33rd IEEE International Conference on Software Analysis, Evolution and Reengineering 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 33rd IEEE International Conference on Software Analysis, Evolution and Reengineering
postings.conferenceText: SANER 2026 is the 33rd IEEE International Conference on Software Analysis, Evolution and Reengineering. The conference focuses on techniques and studies that help recover useful information from existing software, improve maintainability, and support the evolution, migration, and reengineering of software systems. SANER serves as an important forum for researchers and practitioners addressing legacy systems, software quality, and the long-term health of software-intensive systems. Software analysis; evolution and reengineering; reverse engineering; software migration and modernization; maintainability and technical debt; program comprehension and mining; empirical studies of evolving systems; tools and practices for improving existing software.

postings.conferenceName: 25th ACM SIGGRAPH / Eurographics Symposium on Computer Animation 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 25th ACM SIGGRAPH / Eurographics Symposium on Computer Animation
postings.conferenceText: SCA 2026 is the 25th ACM SIGGRAPH / Eurographics Symposium on Computer Animation, a premier forum for research in computer animation. The symposium highlights advances in the modeling, control, simulation, and rendering of time-varying phenomena, as well as character animation, motion generation, and related interactive techniques. The 2026 edition in Barcelona continues the conference’s long-standing role in connecting graphics, physics-based simulation, robotics-inspired motion methods, and animation applications. Computer animation; character animation and control; physics-based simulation; cloth, fluids and deformable objects; motion capture and motion synthesis; data-driven and learning-based animation; crowds and behavioral animation; virtual characters and embodied agents; interactive animation systems; animation for graphics, games and immersive media.

postings.conferenceName: 26th IEEE International Conference on Source Code Analysis and Manipulation 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 26th IEEE International Conference on Source Code Analysis and Manipulation
postings.conferenceText: SCAM 2026 is the 26th IEEE International Conference on Source Code Analysis and Manipulation, an established venue for research on understanding, analyzing, transforming, and exploiting source code and related software artifacts. The conference focuses on source code as a precise representation of software behavior and structure, and on the methods and tools that support maintenance, evolution, quality assurance, and program comprehension. The 2026 edition is co-located with ICSME in Benevento, Italy. Research topics include static and dynamic analysis, program transformation, reverse engineering, code querying, software repository mining, language-aware tooling, refactoring, clone and bug detection, empirical studies on source code, engineering tools for code manipulation, and practical techniques that support comprehension, maintenance, and modern software evolution workflows.

postings.conferenceName: 21st Conference on Sustainable Development of Energy, Water and Environment Systems 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 21st Conference on Sustainable Development of Energy, Water and Environment Systems
postings.conferenceText: The SDEWES conference series is a well-established international forum on the sustainable development of energy, water and environment systems, with strong emphasis on systems thinking, sector coupling and sustainability transitions. The 21st edition, to be held in Gran Canaria, continues the conference’s interdisciplinary tradition by connecting energy engineering, environmental management, urban systems, water systems and policy analysis. The official call for papers highlights the conference as a venue for both methodological and application-oriented work, including smart energy systems, integration of renewables, storage, mobility, circular economy, industrial decarbonization, urban sustainability, and decision support for low-carbon development. Its scope makes it especially relevant to researchers working across technical, environmental and socio-economic dimensions of the energy transition. Methods, tools and approaches for sustainability; green economy, governance and just transition; smart energy systems and sector coupling; energy system analysis, planning and optimization; water-energy nexus and integrated water systems; sustainable urbanism; energy and climate policy; environmental policy and management; renewable resources and conversion technologies; district heating and cooling; biofuels and alternative fuels; electric vehicles and transport; water treatment and desalination; waste and wastewater systems; thermal and electrical storage; smart grids; hydrogen transport; buildings and industrial decarbonization; climate neutrality pathways and related special-session topics.

postings.conferenceName: 41st International Conference on Information Security and Privacy Protection 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 41st International Conference on Information Security and Privacy Protection
postings.conferenceText: IFIP SEC 2026 is the 41st edition of the IFIP TC11 conference on Information Security and Privacy Protection, one of the established international venues in the field. The conference aims to bring together researchers, practitioners, industry, and government participants to discuss current and emerging challenges in ICT security and privacy. Hosted in Perth by Edith Cowan University, SEC 2026 continues the long-running IFIP SEC series and publishes its proceedings in Springer. Theoretical and practical aspects of ICT security and privacy protection; security engineering; privacy-preserving systems; applied cryptography; identity and access management; network and systems security; socio-technical security; security management, governance, and policy; security for cloud, mobile, and critical infrastructures; security measurement, assurance, and real-world case studies.

postings.conferenceName: 22nd EAI International Conference on Security and Privacy in Communication Networks 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 22nd EAI International Conference on Security and Privacy in Communication Networks
postings.conferenceText: SecureComm 2026 is the 22nd EAI International Conference on Security and Privacy in Communication Networks. The conference focuses on cybersecurity and the security and privacy of communication and networking systems, providing a venue for both foundational research and applied results. The 2026 edition will be held in Lancaster in hybrid format and continues the SecureComm series as a forum for researchers and practitioners working on secure communications and trustworthy networked systems. Security and privacy in communication networks; secure networking protocols; wireless, mobile, and IoT security; network defense and attack analysis; applied cryptography for communications; authentication and authorization; privacy-preserving communications; systems and platform security; cyber threat detection and response; security for emerging networked and distributed environments.

postings.conferenceName: 18th International Conference on Sustainable Energy & Environmental Protection 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 18th International Conference on Sustainable Energy & Environmental Protection
postings.conferenceText: The Sustainable Energy & Environmental Protection (SEEP) conference series is an established international forum dedicated to clean energy, environmental protection and sustainable development. The 18th edition is hosted by the University of Rome Tor Vergata and continues SEEP’s role in bringing together academic researchers, industry professionals and policy-oriented participants who work on energy technologies, environmental sustainability and low-carbon solutions. The official website presents the conference as a place for presenting peer-reviewed research, networking and interdisciplinary discussion, with keynote talks, technical sessions and proceedings publication. SEEP is particularly relevant for work that connects engineering solutions with environmental performance and sustainability outcomes. Sustainable energy technologies; environmental protection and sustainability; renewable energy systems; low-carbon engineering solutions; interactions between energy, environment and policy; conference papers, keynote themes and technical-session topics related to clean energy and environmental improvement as reflected on the official conference site.

postings.conferenceName: 22nd International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 22nd International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies
postings.conferenceText: The 22nd International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies (SET2026) is a long-running conference series dedicated to practical and research-driven solutions for sustainable energy and the built environment. According to the official website, the series has been held annually since 2002 and has developed into an international platform for engineers, scientists and policy-oriented participants working on renewable energy, energy efficiency, low-carbon buildings, urban sustainability and environmental stewardship. The 2026 edition is being organized in Kuala Lumpur and continues this tradition by focusing on technologies and strategies that support sustainable development, decarbonization and implementation of cleaner energy systems in real-world contexts. AI-enhanced energy technologies and renewable systems; energy storage and conversion; low-carbon building design and sustainable architectural practices; sustainable urban development, environmental stewardship and city planning; policies and management in sustainable energy; broader sustainable energy technology research, implementation and management issues reflected in the official conference themes.

postings.conferenceName: SETAC Europe 36th Annual Meeting 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: SETAC Europe 36th Annual Meeting
postings.conferenceText: The SETAC Europe 36th Annual Meeting is a major international conference for environmental toxicology, chemistry, exposure science, risk assessment, life cycle thinking, and environmental policy. The 2026 meeting in Maastricht is organized around the theme “Embrace the outlier. In science, regulations and networks,” underscoring the role of novel findings, interdisciplinary thinking, and collaboration in addressing environmental challenges. SETAC’s annual meetings are widely used by researchers, regulators, consultants, industry scientists, and public-sector specialists to present new research, discuss regulatory science, and connect fundamental environmental studies with real-world decision-making. The official programme structure shows a broad environmental focus spanning chemical fate and exposure, toxicological effects, ecological protection, human health, life cycle approaches, policy, management, and cross-cutting emerging topics. Environmental and human toxicology in changing climates; omics, biomarkers and novel methods in ecotoxicology; stress ecology and multiple stressors; environmental chemistry and exposure assessment; monitoring, modelling and chemical fate; ecological and human health risk assessment; life cycle assessment, life cycle management and footprinting; environmental policy, risk management and science communication; cross-cutting, emerging, transdisciplinary and outlying topics in environmental science and regulation.

postings.conferenceName: The 11th International Symposium on Dependable Software Engineering: Theories, Tools and Applications 2025
postings.conferenceSeries: The 11th International Symposium on Dependable Software Engineering: Theories, Tools and Applications
postings.conferenceText: SETTA is an international symposium on dependable software engineering, bringing together work on theories, tools, and applications for building trustworthy software systems. The 2025 meeting at the University of Oxford marks the 11th edition of the series and serves as a forum for researchers interested in rigor, reliability, and formal engineering approaches. Although the homepage is concise, the series positioning clearly emphasizes dependable software engineering across methods, tools, and applications. Dependable software engineering; theories, tools, and applications for trustworthy software; formal reasoning, verification, analysis, and dependable system development.

postings.conferenceName: Symposium on Geometry Processing 2026 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: Symposium on Geometry Processing 2026
postings.conferenceText: SGP 2026 is the Symposium on Geometry Processing 2026, a leading venue for new research on the computational treatment of geometric data. The symposium brings together work on the mathematical, algorithmic, and practical foundations of geometry processing, linking computer graphics, geometric modeling, vision, fabrication, and related areas. The 2026 edition in Bern continues the series’ role as a core meeting point for geometry-focused research and applications. Geometry processing; geometric modeling and shape analysis; meshes, point clouds and implicit representations; parameterization and remeshing; deformation, editing and simulation of geometry; geometric deep learning; reconstruction and acquisition; geometry for fabrication and digital manufacturing; geometry in graphics, vision and scientific computing.

postings.conferenceName: ACM SIGCOMM 2026 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: ACM SIGCOMM 2026
postings.conferenceText: ACM SIGCOMM 2026 is the flagship annual conference of ACM SIGCOMM and one of the most important venues in data communication and networking. The conference seeks significant research contributions and significant deployment experiences in communication networks and networked systems, and the 2026 edition is held at the Colorado Convention Center in Denver, Colorado. The conference accepts both research and experience papers and continues SIGCOMM's role as a premier forum for networking research. According to the official call for papers, SIGCOMM takes a broad view of networking, including all types of computer networks (mobile, wide-area, datacenter, embedded, home, and enterprise), all wired and wireless technologies (optics, radio, acoustic, visible-light communication), and all aspects of networked systems such as architecture, packet- and circuit-switched hardware and software, virtualization, mobility, resource management, performance, energy and environmental impact, topology, robustness, security, diagnosis, verification, privacy, economics, evolution, and interactions with applications. It also welcomes all parts of the network lifecycle and all approaches including theory, analysis, experimentation, and AI/machine learning for networking.

postings.conferenceName: SIGGRAPH 2026: The 53rd International Conference & Exhibition on Computer Graphics & Interactive Techniques 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: SIGGRAPH 2026: The 53rd International Conference & Exhibition on Computer Graphics & Interactive Techniques

postings.conferenceName: ACM SIGMETRICS 2026 2026

postings.conferenceName: ACM SIGMOD/PODS International Conference on Management of Data 2027

Database systems and architectures; query processing and optimization; transaction processing and concurrency control; data integration and data cleaning; graph, stream and spatial data management; large-scale analytics; cloud and distributed data systems; ML/AI for data management and data management for AI workloads; data privacy, security and responsible data systems.

postings.conferenceText: SMI is an international forum for new mathematical theories and computational techniques for modeling, simulating, and processing digital representations of shapes and their properties. postings.conferenceName: ACM Symposium on Cloud Computing 2026 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: ACM Symposium on Cloud Computing 2026

postings.conferenceName: ACM-SIAM Symposium on Discrete Algorithms 2027
postings.conferenceSeries: ACM-SIAM Symposium on Discrete Algorithms
postings.conferenceText: SODA 2027 is the ACM-SIAM Symposium on Discrete Algorithms, a premier venue for research on the design, analysis, and applications of discrete algorithms. postings.conferenceName: 32nd SolarPACES Conference 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 32nd SolarPACES Conference

Concentrating solar thermal power and power cycles; collectors, receivers and thermal systems; thermal energy storage; operations and maintenance; simulation, modelling and digital tools including AI; hybrid systems and grid integration; solar process heat and desalination; market development, policy and commercial projects; solar resource assessment and measurement systems; advanced materials and coatings; solar fuels, solar chemistry and high-temperature thermochemical processes.

postings.conferenceName: 38th ACM Symposium on Parallelism in Algorithms and Architectures 2026

postings.conferenceName: 28th International Conference on Speech and Computer 2026

postings.conferenceName: Symposium on Solid and Physical Modeling 2025

postings.conferenceName: 58th ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing 2026

postings.conferenceText: STOC 2026 is the 58th ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing, one of the flagship conferences in theoretical computer science. postings.conferenceText: The 10th Edition of International Conference on Traditional Medicine and Integrative Health bridges traditional medicine and modern healthcare in Rome and Online from June 24-26, 2027, with sixteen tracks over three days. Every part of the programme is directed at bringing traditional knowledge and clinical evidence together in ways that benefit scholars, practitioners, and public-health professionals. Coverage at this Holistic Medicine Conference 2027 reaches across Traditional Chinese Medicine, Ayurveda, acupuncture, herbal medicine, phytotherapy, mind-body therapies, yoga and meditation, aromatherapy and music therapy, biofeedback mechanisms, natural therapies, holistic treatment, cultural preservation in medicine, modern-healthcare integration, and global-health integration. Within the Traditional Medicine Conferences 2027 calendar, this meeting operates a tiered registration model - abstract submission for speakers and presenters, standard or early-bird rates for delegates and listeners. postings.conferenceSeries: 23rd International Workshop on Trust, Privacy and Security in the Digital Society
postings.conferenceText: TrustBus 2026 is the 23rd International Workshop on Trust, Privacy and Security in the Digital Society and will be held in conjunction with ARES 2026. The official workshop page describes TrustBus as a long-running international and interdisciplinary forum, with a series dating back to 2004, where researchers and practitioners exchange advances in the state of the art and practice of trust, privacy, and security. The 2026 edition frames its scope in the context of a rapidly evolving digital society shaped by generative AI, cloud and edge computing, and the Internet of Things. The workshop emphasizes both technical innovation and the broader societal, legal, and regulatory environment in which digital trust and security challenges arise. As a co-located workshop within ARES, it sits at the intersection of dependable systems, privacy protection, and secure digital services. Accountability, transparency and intervenability; anonymity and pseudonymity; common practices, legal and regulatory issues; detecting and preventing digital misinformation; economics of cyber security and privacy; identity management, identity theft and trust management; information audit and trust; reliable auction, e-procurement and negotiation technology; security and privacy for cloud and edge computing; security and privacy in data governance and management; security and privacy patterns and antipatterns; security, privacy and trust for digital society services; security, privacy and trust in mobile environments; supply chain cyber security; trust and reputation for digital societies; trustworthy AI; usability of security and privacy technologies and services.

postings.conferenceName: 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
postings.conferenceText: UAI 2026 is the 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, a premier conference devoted to knowledge representation, learning, and reasoning under uncertainty. Since 1985, the series has brought together the community working on probabilistic reasoning, causal inference, structured models, decision making, and statistically grounded AI methods. The 2026 edition takes place in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with tutorials and workshops surrounding the main conference. The conference focuses on uncertainty in artificial intelligence, including probabilistic modeling, Bayesian methods, causal reasoning, decision making, inference and learning under uncertainty, structured representations, and related theoretical and application-driven advances.

postings.conferenceName: UbiComp / ISWC 2026 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: UbiComp / ISWC 2026
postings.conferenceText: UbiComp / ISWC 2026 is the joint conference for ubiquitous computing and wearable computing, bringing together the communities behind two influential ACM conference series. The event covers the design, implementation, and study of technologies embedded in everyday environments, devices, and interactions, from pervasive sensing to human-centered wearable systems. The 2026 edition in Shanghai continues the joint conference’s role as a hub for innovative, interdisciplinary work spanning systems, interaction, health, intelligence, and real-world deployment. Ubiquitous and pervasive computing; wearable computing and sensing; mobile and context-aware systems; IoT and smart environments; human-centered AI in everyday settings; health, wellbeing and assistive technologies; privacy, ethics and trust in ubiquitous systems; interaction techniques and user studies; real-world deployments and longitudinal evaluations.

postings.conferenceName: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
postings.conferenceText: UIST 2026 is the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology, a premier forum for innovations in human-computer interfaces. The symposium showcases advances in the software and hardware of interactive systems, including novel interaction techniques, input/output technologies, toolkits, and applied interface systems. The 2026 edition in Detroit continues UIST’s strong tradition of presenting influential, forward-looking work on interactive technologies. User interface software and technology; innovative interaction techniques; hardware and sensing for interfaces; toolkits and systems for interactive computing; novel input/output methods; prototyping, design, and evaluation of next-generation interactive technologies.

postings.conferenceName: 61st International Universities Power Engineering Conference 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 61st International Universities Power Engineering Conference
postings.conferenceText: The 61st International Universities Power Engineering Conference (UPEC 2026) is a long-running international forum on electric power engineering hosted by the University of Cagliari. The 2026 conference is framed around the theme “Bridging Power Engineering Heritage and the AI-Driven Energy Future,” positioning the event as a venue for both classical and emerging topics in modern power systems. UPEC traditionally gathers researchers, academics, students, and industry participants working across power generation, transmission, distribution, power electronics, system operation, and digital energy technologies. The conference particularly emphasizes the interaction between established power engineering methods and newer developments such as artificial intelligence, data-driven operation, flexible energy systems, and resilient pathways toward a carbon-neutral energy future. Artificial intelligence in power system operation; planning, control and forecasting; intelligent management of grids and distributed energy resources; resilience, flexibility and sustainability of energy systems; conventional and renewable power engineering; smart grids; power electronics; system analysis, operation and optimization; future low-carbon electricity infrastructures and AI-enabled energy technologies.

postings.conferenceName: 36th USENIX Security Symposium 2027
postings.conferenceSeries: 36th USENIX Security Symposium
postings.conferenceText: The 36th USENIX Security Symposium is a flagship venue for advances in the security and privacy of computer systems and networks. The symposium brings together research on attacks, defenses, secure systems design, privacy technologies, and the empirical study of security in practice. The 2027 edition is scheduled in Denver, Colorado and continues the USENIX Security tradition as one of the most influential conferences in computer security. The symposium broadly covers systems and network security, privacy, applied cryptography, software and hardware security, web and mobile security, secure machine learning, measurement studies, usable security, offensive and defensive techniques, and practical evaluations of security and privacy technologies. The homepage lists two submission cycles; this record captures cycle 1.

postings.conferenceName: 53rd International Conference on Very Large Data Bases 2027
postings.conferenceSeries: 53rd International Conference on Very Large Data Bases
postings.conferenceText: VLDB 2027 is the 53rd International Conference on Very Large Data Bases, one of the flagship conferences in data management. The conference advances the state of the art in data systems, data-intensive applications, and large-scale information processing, and has a long history of publishing influential work at the intersection of theory, systems, and practice. The 2027 edition in Athens continues VLDB’s role as a major international venue for innovations in modern data infrastructure. Database systems; data processing at scale; query optimization and execution; cloud and distributed data management; graph, streaming and spatial data; analytics and data science systems; data management for machine learning and AI; transaction processing and consistency; data integration and information quality; privacy, security and responsible data systems.

postings.conferenceName: 27th International Conference on Verification, Model Checking, and Abstract Interpretation 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 27th International Conference on Verification, Model Checking, and Abstract Interpretation
postings.conferenceText: VMCAI 2026 is the 27th International Conference on Verification, Model Checking, and Abstract Interpretation. The conference provides a forum for researchers from the verification, model checking, and abstract interpretation communities, with a strong emphasis on connections between formal reasoning techniques and practical analysis methods. Co-located with POPL, VMCAI covers sound static and dynamic methods for analyzing programs and systems. Verification; model checking; abstract interpretation; static and dynamic analysis; program semantics; formal reasoning about software and systems; hybrid analysis methods; tool support for rigorous analysis.

postings.conferenceName: The IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision 2026 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: The IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision 2026
postings.conferenceText: WACV is a premier international computer vision conference organized by the IEEE Computer Society and the Computer Vision Foundation. The 2026 edition is held in Tucson, Arizona and combines the main conference with co-located workshops, tutorials, demos, a doctoral consortium, and poster activities. The conference emphasizes high-quality, high-impact work in applications of computer vision, giving students, academic researchers, and industry practitioners a focused venue for presenting new results, discussing emerging directions, and engaging with the broader vision community. Computer vision research and applications; vision systems and real-world deployments; visual recognition and scene understanding; detection, segmentation, tracking, and video analysis; 3D vision, geometry, and multimodal perception; open review paper tracks with workshops, tutorials, demos, and doctoral consortium contributions.

postings.conferenceName: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference
postings.conferenceText: IEEE WCNC is a flagship conference of the IEEE Communications Society and a top-ranked venue for wireless communications and networking research. The 2026 edition is hosted in Kuala Lumpur and features a comprehensive in-person program including technical papers, workshops, tutorials, panels, keynote speeches, and industry exhibits. The conference is aimed at researchers from academia, industry, and government working on cutting-edge technologies, applications, and services across wireless systems and networks. Wireless communications and networking; technical papers; workshops; tutorials; panel proposals; submission guidelines for communications systems, networking technologies, applications, and services across modern wireless ecosystems.

postings.conferenceName: The 9th Annual World Congress of Smart Materials 2025
postings.conferenceSeries: The 9th Annual World Congress of Smart Materials
postings.conferenceText: The 9th Annual World Congress of Smart Materials (WCSM-2025) is an international congress dedicated to the design, development, engineering, and applications of smart materials. The official site positions smart materials as an important direction within advanced high-technology materials research and presents the congress as a platform for exchange between academia, research institutes, and industry. The 2025 edition will be held in Osaka, Japan and is organized through multiple thematic forums that cover both core materials science and practical applications. The congress aims to encourage interdisciplinary dialogue on how smart materials can enable future technologies in manufacturing, optics, electronics, energy, environment, biomedicine, and intelligent structures. Forum themes include smart materials engineering, mechanical and manufacturing topics; smart optical, electronic and magnetic materials; smart materials for energy and environment; smart biomaterials and bio-engineering; smart materials and structures; and future trends and applications of smart materials. The program also covers related subtopics in design, synthesis, functionality, characterization, integration, devices, and application-driven development.

postings.conferenceName: WEFTEC 2026 – 99th Annual Technical Exhibition & Conference 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: WEFTEC 2026 – 99th Annual Technical Exhibition & Conference
postings.conferenceText: WEFTEC is the flagship annual technical exhibition and conference of the Water Environment Federation and is one of the most established international events in the water and wastewater sector. The 2026 edition in New Orleans continues the long-running series as its 99th annual meeting. The conference brings together utility professionals, engineers, technology providers, researchers, operators, regulators and consultants to exchange practical and research-driven advances in water quality management, wastewater treatment, resource recovery, infrastructure, operations, and environmental protection. The official programme highlights workshops, technical sessions, facility tours, and continuing education opportunities, reflecting WEFTEC’s role as a major forum for professional training, technology demonstration, and discussion of emerging issues in water environment engineering. Water quality and wastewater engineering; treatment processes and plant operations; collection systems and sewer infrastructure; residuals, biosolids and resource recovery; stormwater and wet weather management; utility management and asset planning; environmental compliance and regulation; process control, digitalization and monitoring; facility tours, workshops, posters and technical sessions related to the water environment field.

postings.conferenceName: 25th World Hydrogen Energy Conference 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 25th World Hydrogen Energy Conference
postings.conferenceText: The 25th World Hydrogen Energy Conference (WHEC 2026) is an established international conference series dedicated to the hydrogen economy and the engineering, science and policy required for large-scale deployment of hydrogen technologies. The 2026 edition in Singapore brings together researchers, industry leaders, policy specialists and technology developers to discuss how hydrogen can support decarbonization, industrial transformation and resilient energy systems. The official programme emphasizes cross-sector collaboration and addresses the full hydrogen value chain, from production and infrastructure to safety, utilization, economics and regional deployment. As a global hydrogen conference with a long history, WHEC functions as a major forum for linking fundamental advances with practical implementation and market creation. Hydrogen production, electrolysis and alternative pathways; hydrogen transport, storage and distribution; fuel cells and hydrogen end-use applications; safety, standards and codes; systems integration and energy infrastructure; techno-economics, commercialization and policy; materials, components and manufacturing for hydrogen technologies; mobility and transport applications; industrial decarbonization; regional hydrogen deployment strategies and broader hydrogen economy development topics organized under the official WHEC topic groups.

postings.conferenceName: 19th EAI International Conference on Wireless Internet 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 19th EAI International Conference on Wireless Internet
postings.conferenceText: WiCON 2026 is the 19th EAI International Conference on Wireless Internet. The conference focuses on architectures, protocols, systems, and applications for wireless and mobile Internet technologies, connecting networking foundations with evolving service and platform needs. The 2026 edition in Bratislava continues the conference’s emphasis on practical and research advances in pervasive wireless connectivity, network intelligence, and future communication environments. Wireless Internet architectures; mobile and cellular networking; IoT and sensor networks; edge and pervasive wireless systems; routing, mobility and protocol design; performance, management and optimization; security and privacy in wireless Internet; AI/ML for wireless networking; emerging applications over mobile and wireless platforms.

postings.conferenceName: 19th ACM Conference on Security and Privacy in Wireless and Mobile Networks 2026
postings.conferenceSeries: 19th ACM Conference on Security and Privacy in Wireless and Mobile Networks
postings.conferenceText: WiSec 2026 is the 19th ACM Conference on Security and Privacy in Wireless and Mobile Networks. The conference is a leading venue for research on security and privacy issues in wireless communications, mobile systems, IoT, cyber-physical environments, and related applications. Hosted by CISPA in Saarbrücken, WiSec combines foundational methods with practical defenses and system-building work relevant to contemporary networked platforms. Wireless and mobile security; cellular and network protocol security; IoT and cyber-physical systems security; privacy in mobile and wireless systems; applied cryptography for wireless settings; authentication and access control; usable security and privacy; biometrics; attacks, measurements, and defenses for connected devices and platforms.

postings.conferenceName: 3rd World Materials Conference / 9th World Materials Summit / 26th IUMRS-ICA 2025 2025
postings.conferenceSeries: 3rd World Materials Conference / 9th World Materials Summit / 26th IUMRS-ICA 2025
postings.conferenceText: This official conference site presents a combined materials event consisting of the 3rd World Materials Conference (WMC 2025), the 9th World Materials Summit (WMS 2025), and the 26th International Conference in Asia of the International Union of Materials Research Societies (IUMRS-ICA 2025). Hosted in Guilin, China, the meeting is organized around international exchange in advanced materials research and development, with participation from the broader global materials community. The conference and summit format brings together academic presentations, strategic discussion on the future of materials science and engineering, and cross-regional collaboration among major materials research organizations. The event is positioned as a broad platform covering leading topics across modern materials research, innovation, and applications. Advanced materials research and engineering; international materials collaboration; structural and functional materials; energy and environmental materials; electronic and optical materials; biomaterials and soft materials; materials processing and manufacturing; materials characterization; frontier materials technologies; strategic summit discussions on materials innovation and future directions; and technical sessions associated with the WMC, WMS and IUMRS-ICA programs.

The 2026 edition is held in Dubai, United Arab Emirates and features research sessions, posters and demos, a PhD symposium, workshops, tutorials, special tracks, industry activities, keynote talks, panels, and the co-located Web4All event. postings.conferenceText: Call for papers/TopicsAll Abstracts, Reviews, short articles, Full articles, Posters are welcomed related with any of the following research fields:Foundational & Independent TopicsThese topics represent the core architectural, physical, and algorithmic principles unique to each standalone discipline.1. Computing and Computer ScienceThe study of algorithmic processes, software design, and information representation. Data Structures and Algorithms: Linear and non-linear data structures, sorting and searching algorithms, and computational complexity (Big O notation). Theory of Computation: Automata theory, formal languages, computability theory, and Turing machines. Software Engineering and Architecture: Object-oriented design, software development lifecycles (Agile, DevOps), design patterns, and microservices architecture. Database Systems: Relational database management systems (RDBMS), NoSQL frameworks, query optimization, and data warehousing. Operating Systems: Process management, memory allocation, file systems, concurrency, and virtualization. 2. Core Engineering PrinciplesThe physical and mathematical foundations used to design and analyze hardware and structural systems. Circuit Theory and Electronics: Analog and digital circuits, semiconductor devices, operational amplifiers, and signal conditioning. Signals and Systems: Continuous and discrete-time signals, Fourier transforms, and linear time-invariant (LTI) systems. Control Systems: Feedback loops, PID controllers, system stability analysis, and state-space modeling. Digital Signal Processing (DSP): Sampling theory, digital filtering, and spectral analysis. 3. Core CybersecurityThe specialized methodologies used to protect data, identity, and assets from unauthorized access or damage. Cryptography Foundations: Symmetric and asymmetric encryption, cryptographic hashing, digital signatures, and public key infrastructure (PKI). Identity and Access Management (IAM): Multi-factor authentication, role-based access control (RBAC), single sign-on (SSO), and directory services. Threat and Vulnerability Management: Penetration testing methodologies, vulnerability scanning, risk assessment frameworks, and common vulnerability scoring. Incident Response and Digital Forensics: Log analysis, malware analysis, chain of custody procedures, and disaster recovery planning. Interrelated & Integrated TopicsThese fields represent the spaces where computing, physical engineering, and security merge to build resilient digital and physical infrastructures.1. Computer Engineering and Hardware SecurityThe direct intersection of computing and engineering, along with the specialized security required to protect physical chips and components. Computer Architecture and Microprocessors: Instruction set architectures (ISA), pipelining, cache hierarchies, and multi-core processing. Hardware Root of Trust: Trusted Platform Modules (TPM), Secure Enclaves, and physical unclonable functions (PUFs). Side-Channel Attacks and Hardware Exploits: Analyzing power consumption, timing variations, or electromagnetic radiation to extract cryptographic keys, and mitigating hardware bugs (like Spectre or Meltdown). Embedded Systems Design: Microcontrollers, real-time operating systems (RTOS), and hardware-software co-design. 2. Network Engineering and Network SecurityThe integration of computing communication frameworks with the engineering of physical infrastructure and active defensive measures. Network Architectures and Protocols: Routing protocols (BGP, OSPF), the OSI and TCP/IP models, and Software-Defined Networking (SDN). Network Defensive Architectures: Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW), Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS), and demilitarized zones (DMZs). Wireless and Mobile Network Security: Wi-Fi encryption protocols (WPA3), cellular network generation architectures (5G/6G), and rogue access point detection. Zero Trust Network Architecture (ZTNA): Micro-segmentation, continuous verification, and perimeter-less security frameworks. 3. Cyber-Physical Systems and Industrial SecurityThe convergence of physical control engineering with computing networks, presenting highly unique security environments. Internet of Things (IoT) Engineering: Low-power wide-area networks (LPWAN), edge computing, firmware optimization, and IoT device hardening. Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and SCADA Security: Modbus/DNP3 protocol vulnerabilities, network isolation, the Purdue Model for industrial control, and protecting critical infrastructure (power grids, water systems). Robotics and Autonomous Vehicle Security: Securing Controller Area Network (CAN) buses in automobiles, securing drone telemetry links, and preventing sensor spoofing. 4. Cloud Computing and Cloud SecurityThe deployment of enterprise computing and engineering infrastructure abstracted into virtual environments, requiring distinct security frameworks. Cloud Infrastructure Architecture: Infrastructure as Code (IaC), containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), and serverless computing. Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM): Misconfiguration detection, compliance monitoring across multi-cloud environments, and cloud IAM. DevSecOps Implementation: Automating security testing within continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) software pipelines

postings.conferenceText: Call for papers/TopicsTopics of interest for submission include any topics related to:1. Independent Core DisciplinesThese represent the foundational pillars of each distinct field before they intersect with one another.Social Sciences Sociology: Social stratification, institutional structures, deviance, socialization, and collective behavior. Anthropology: Cultural anthropology, ethnography, archaeology, linguistic anthropology, and human evolution. Political Science: Comparative politics, international relations, political theory, public policy, and electoral systems. Psychology: Cognitive processes, developmental psychology, abnormal psychology, and behavioral neuroscience. Human Geography: Demographics, urbanization, spatial analysis, and cultural landscapes. Humanities History: Ancient, medieval, and modern world histories, historiography, and archival research. Philosophy: Epistemology, metaphysics, ethics, aesthetics, and formal logic. Literature: Literary theory, textual criticism, poetry, prose, and comparative literature. Linguistics: Phonetics, syntax, semantics, morphology, and historical linguistics. Visual and Performing Arts History: Art history, ethnomusicology, cinema studies, and theater history. Religious Studies: Comparative religion, theology, mythology, and sacred texts. 2. Interrelated Cross-Disciplinary FieldsThese subtopics exist at the intersections where two or more of the core disciplines overlap, blending empirical inquiry with interpretive analysis.History + Sociology/Anthropology Historical Sociology: The study of how societies develop through history and how historical structures shape modern social realities. Social History: The history of ordinary people, daily life, subcultures, and social movements rather than political elites. Ethnohistory: Combining anthropological fieldwork with historical documents to study the history of indigenous cultures. Philosophy + Political Science (The Governance Nexus) Political Philosophy: Intellectual exploration of justice, liberty, property, rights, and the legitimacy of government institutions. Ethics and Public Policy: Applying moral philosophy to contemporary legislative issues, such as bioethics or environmental laws. Philosophy of Social Science: Investigating the logic, methods, and scientific validity of social research. Psychology + Sociology (The Behavioral Nexus) Social Psychology: How individual thoughts, feelings, and behaviors are influenced by the actual or implied presence of others. Sociology of Mental Health: Analyzing how social status, poverty, and institutional frameworks affect psychological well-being. Crowd Psychology: The study of group behavior, mass hysteria, and social movements. Literature/Linguistics + Cultural Anthropology (The Expressive Nexus) Sociolinguistics: The study of how language varies based on social factors like class, gender, ethnicity, and geography. Cultural Studies: Interdisciplinary analysis of modern media, popular culture, consumerism, and ideology. Oral History and Folklore: The collection and analysis of verbal traditions, myths, and personal narratives passed through generations. 3. Advanced Multi-Disciplinary SubtopicsThese complex, contemporary fields synthesize numerous branches of both the social sciences and humanities to address systemic human questions. Digital Humanities: Using computational tools, data science (social science), and digital archiving to analyze literature, historical trends, and artistic developments (humanities). Gender and Sexuality Studies: Blending sociology, history, literature, and psychology to examine how gender roles, identity, and patriarchy are constructed across different times and cultures. Postcolonial Studies: Analyzing the historical, political (social science), literary, and cultural (humanities) legacies of colonial rule and globalization. Environmental Humanities and Ecofeminism: Blending human geography, ethics, history, and literature to explore the cultural and philosophical relationship between humans and the natural world. Memory Studies: Investigating how nations and cultures collectively remember, commemorate, or forget historical events through public monuments (art history), political narratives (political science), and trauma (psychology)

postings.conferenceText: TopicsAll Abstracts, Reviews, short articles, Full articles, Posters are welcomed related with any of the following research fields:Independent Core Domains1. Soil & Terrestrial Systems: Pedogenesis, soil nutrient cycling, terrestrial carbon sequestration, and soil microbiology. Biogeography: Species distribution modeling, phylogeography, evolutionary island biogeography, and climate change migration dynamics. 3. Climate Change & Earth System Science: Ice core paleoclimate reconstruction, sea-level dynamics, feedback loops between soil microbes and atmospheric temperature, and ocean circulation models. postings.conferenceName: 5th PARIS World Conference on Organic Agriculture, Food Security & Public Health (POAFPH-26) Dec. 3-5, 2026 Paris (France)
postings.conferenceText: Call for papers/TopicsTopics of interest for submission include any topics related to:1. Organic Agriculture: This pillar focuses on the methods and ecological standards of food production. Soil Health and Biodiversity Soil microbiome and nutrient cycling. Carbon sequestration and regenerative practices. Crop rotation and polyculture vs. monoculture. Input Management Bio-fertilizers and green manure. Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and botanical pesticides. Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) vs. heirloom seeds. Certification and Economics Global certification standards (USDA, EU Organic, IFOAM). Transition costs for smallholder farmers. The "Organic Premium" and market accessibility. 2. Food Security: This pillar focuses on the availability, access, and stability of the food supply. Production and Availability Yield comparisons: Organic vs. Conventional farming. Resilience of organic systems to climate change (drought and flood resistance). Local vs. Global food supply chains. Accessibility and Equity Food deserts and the cost-prohibitive nature of organic goods. Smallholder farmer livelihoods and food sovereignty. Urban agriculture and community-supported agriculture (CSA). Waste and Stability Post-harvest loss reduction in organic supply chains. Resource efficiency (water use and energy inputs). 3. Public Health: This pillar examines the physiological and environmental impacts of the food system on human health. Nutritional Quality Phytonutrient and antioxidant concentrations in organic produce. Fatty acid profiles (Omega-3 vs. Omega-6) in organic dairy and meat. Bioavailability of micronutrients. Toxicology and Exposure Pesticide residue and endocrine disruption. Antibiotic resistance in livestock and zoonotic diseases. Heavy metal accumulation in soil and crops. Diet-Related Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) Links between organic consumption and obesity/diabetes rates. The "Clean Label" movement and processed food reduction. 4. Interrelated Themes (The Nexus)These topics sit at the overlap of all three fields, driving policy and research. The Microbiome Connection: How organic soil health influences the human gut microbiome via the food we eat. Environmental Health: The reduction of nitrate leaching into groundwater and its impact on community drinking water safety. Climate Change Mitigation: How organic practices reduce the carbon footprint of the food system, thereby protecting long-term food security and reducing climate-related health risks. Policy and Governance: Government subsidies for conventional vs. organic farming and their long-term impact on national healthcare costs. Ethical Consumption: The psychological impact of "food citizenship" and its influence on community mental health and social cohesion.

postings.conferenceText: Call for papers/TopicsAll Abstracts, Reviews, short articles, Full articles, Posters are welcomed related with any of the following research fields:Foundational & Independent TopicsThese areas focus on how technology fundamentally alters the core structures of daily human life, distinct institutional systems, and traditional practices.1. The Impact of Technology on SocietyThe restructuring of civic life, economics, and human interaction through technological advancement. The Future of Work and Automation: The shift from manufacturing to knowledge economies, remote and hybrid work structures, gig economy platforms, and workforce displacement by artificial intelligence. Digital Civics and Governance: E-governance portals, algorithmic bias in public policy, online political mobilization, and surveillance capitalism. Social Connectivity and Isolation: Parasocial relationships via social platforms, the erosion of local physical communities, and the psychological impact of hyper-connectivity. Privacy, Security, and Surveillance: Big data collection, facial recognition technology, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and the monetization of personal identity. 2. The Impact of Technology on CultureThe evolution of human expression, identity formation, and the sharing of values across global networks. Digital Identity and Self-Expression: The curation of online personas, avatar culture, virtual worlds, and the blurring lines between physical and digital reality. Media Consumption and Entertainment: The rise of streaming algorithms, virtual and augmented reality storytelling, user-generated content economies, and the decline of centralized mainstream media. Language and Communication Aesthetics: The emergence of digital-native dialects (memes, emojis, internet slang), shortened attention-span content forms, and instantaneous global translation. Global Homogenization vs. Cultural Preservation: The spread of Western-centric digital ideals versus the use of technology to archive endangered indigenous languages and cultural histories. 3. The Impact of Technology on EducationThe transformation of how knowledge is preserved, transmitted, accessed, and evaluated. Pedagogical Shift to EdTech: Asynchronous learning platforms, flipped classrooms, and adaptive learning software tailored to individual student paces. The Democratization of Knowledge: Open-access academic journals, Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), and the destruction of geographic barriers to elite education. Digital Literacy and Information Fluency: Teaching students how to evaluate source credibility, identify deepfakes, navigate algorithmic confirmation bias, and manage digital wellness. Assessment and Institutional Redesign: Moving away from rote memorization due to ubiquitous information access, restructuring academic integrity policies around artificial intelligence, and the devaluation of traditional four-year degrees in favor of micro-credentials. Interrelated & Overlapping TopicsThese cross-cutting disciplines exist precisely at the intersections of society, culture, and education, where a change in one domain triggers a ripple effect across the others.1. The Digital Divide and Socio-Economic InequalityIntersection of Society, Culture, and Education Infrastructure Disparities: How unequal access to high-speed broadband and hardware reinforces class divides in education and limits upward economic mobility in society. Cultural Capital in the Digital Age: The gap between basic digital literacy (using a smartphone for entertainment) and advanced digital literacy (using technology for creation, programming, and financial growth). Global Knowledge Stratification: The concentration of technological ownership in specific geographic hubs, creating educational and cultural dependencies for developing nations. 2. Artificial Intelligence Ethics and the Human ExperienceIntersection of Society and Culture Algorithmic Bias and Discrimination: How AI models trained on historical data replicate systemic social prejudices in hiring practices, judicial systems, and cultural representations. The Philosophy of Human Labor and Creativity: AI-generated art, music, and literature challenging the cultural definition of unique human creativity, while simultaneously disrupting creative career paths in society. Cognitive Offloading: The societal and cultural implications of outsourcing memory, decision-making, and critical analysis to algorithmic assistants. 3. Misinformation, Polarization, and Public DiscourseIntersection of Society, Culture, and Education Echo Chambers and Filter Bubbles: How social media algorithms maximize engagement by feeding users polarizing content, fracturing shared cultural narratives, and destabilizing democratic societies. The Post-Truth Era: The cultural normalization of skepticism toward established scientific and journalistic institutions, demanding immediate educational updates to media literacy curriculums. Information Warfare: State-sponsored digital disinformation campaigns targeting societal stability and exploiting cultural vulnerabilities. 4. Digital Health, Well-being, and DevelopmentIntersection of Society and Education Screen Time and Child Development: Educational challenges arising from attentional deficits, sleep disruption, and decreased face-to-face social skills in younger generations. The Economy of Attention: How platforms purposefully design psychological hooks (dopamine feedback loops) that compete directly with institutional educational goals and productive societal engagement.

postings.conferenceText: The Global Surgical Science & Technology Conference (GSST 2026) Hybrid Event is an internationally recognized forum dedicated to advancing research, innovation, and technological progress in the field of surgery. Taking place from October 26–28, 2026, in Boston, Massachusetts, USA, the conference will also be accessible online, providing a fully integrated hybrid experience that facilitates participation and collaboration across the globe.Surgery Conference 2026 brings together a diverse community of professionals, including surgical specialists, clinical investigators, biomedical engineers, healthcare researchers, academic faculty, and industry leaders. The event is structured to encourage interdisciplinary interaction, enabling attendees to exchange insights on emerging innovations, practical applications, and novel strategies that enhance surgical accuracy, efficiency, and patient-centered outcomes.The Surgical Science Conference is designed to address the most significant and emerging topics in surgical science and technology. Key areas of focus include minimally invasive and robotic-assisted procedures, AI-enabled surgical planning, development of advanced instruments and medical devices, regenerative medicine, personalized treatment solutions, optimization of perioperative care, and innovative approaches to surgical education and skill development. Sessions will feature a combination of keynote speeches, expert-led panel discussions, oral and poster presentations, interactive workshops, and collaborative forums that integrate research findings with clinical practice.Contributors are invited to submit original research, clinical studies, case reports, systematic reviews, and innovative technological solutions. Accepted submissions will be showcased in official conference proceedings, providing international exposure and opportunities for professional networking. The Surgery Conferences ensures that both in-person and virtual participants can engage in live presentations, interactive discussions, and on-demand content throughout the event.By promoting global collaboration, interdisciplinary knowledge exchange, and technological innovation, GSST 2026 seeks to drive progress in surgical science, support evidence-based practice, and inspire the next generation of advancements in patient care. The conference provides a strategic platform for presenting research, fostering connections, and remaining at the forefront of developments shaping modern surgical practice.

postings.conferenceName: 1st International Workshop on Analysis of Broad Dynamic Topics over Social Media (Co-located with ECIR 2018)
postings.conferenceText: You are invited to submit your research work to the 1st International Workshop on Analysis of Broad Dynamic Topics over Social Media (BroDyn ’18), to be held at Grenoble, France, on March 26th 2018, in conjunction with the 40th European Conference on Information Retrieval (ECIR 2018).Find more information on our website (https://sites.google.com/view/brodyn2018) and follow us on Twitter @BroDyn2018.**Motivation and OverviewIn recent years, users developed a widespread perception of social media as news sources that they follow (almost all day long) to get updated on their topics of interest. Many of those topics attract long-standing user interest (i.e., span or stay active for long period of time), are very broad (i.e., cover many aspects or subtopics), and are dynamic (i.e., develop and change focus over time with subtopics becoming obsolete over time and new subtopics emerge). Such kind of broad and dynamic topics can run for few weeks, such as crisis events (e.g., “Hurricane Irma”), or up to years, such as “the Syrian conflict”. Other examples of broad dynamic topics include “Refugees in Europe”, “Qatar Crisis”, “Brexit”, “North Korea and US conflict” to name a few.Effective exploitation of content posted on social media that is relevant to broad dynamic topics requires adaptive techniques to effectively capture the different and changing aspects of the topics. The techniques should also be scalable to cope with the large volume of posts and the diversity of the sub-topics, real-time to be responsive to the high velocity of the data, and reliable to perform effectively over the long duration of the topic. In addition to that, new evaluation frameworks for such domain are also needed with novel evaluation measures that capture the nature of topics (and thus systems) and new large reusable datasets that enable the researchers to run meaningful and representative experiments.The workshop aims to bring together audience at all levels, including researchers from academia and industry as well as potential users, to create a forum for discussing recent advances in this emerging area. The theme of the workshop concerns, besides IR and social computing researchers, a wide spectrum of potential users of the needed technology, such as journalists, historians, politicians, social scientists and analysts.**Workshop AimsBroDyn workshop aims to achieve the following objectives:1. Directing the attention of IR researchers to the new emerging type of information needs that require following broad and dynamic topics and events over social media streams.2. Better understanding of the limitations of the current methods and inspiring research on new algorithms and techniques.3. Encouraging the design of new evaluation measures, datasets, and test collections to support the research in that area.4. Forming a new community that brings together IR and social computing researchers as well as potential users who are interested in the domain.**Topics of InterestWe encourage submissions on all topics related to the theme of analysis of broad and dynamic topics over social media, focused on (but not limited to) the following tasks:- Adaptive high-recall high-precision filtering / topic tracking- Adaptive summarization- Topic/sub-topic or event/sub-event detection over time- Retrospective generation of timelines- Following controversial political events/crises: identification of decision makers, credibility/information source finding, stance/opinion mining, troll detection, fact checking- Cross-media filtering (i.e., over heterogeneous sources)- Multilingual topic/event detection- Online/dynamic topic modeling- Real-time/scalable techniques of processing high-volume streams- Evaluation techniques and novel test collections (specific for broad dynamic topics)- Spam and hashtag-spam detection- Bot and automatically-generated content detection- Data visualization- Recommendation (e.g., of hashtags/topics/sub-topics)- Learning techniques/deep learning over social streams**Available DatasetsWe encourage (but not require) submissions describing experiments using the GE2017 (a dataset of around 18M tweets on the British General Elections 2017) and/or USPresElect2016 (a dataset of 3,450 labelled tweets on the US Presidential Elections 2016). Find more details on our website.**SubmissionsWe are seeking the submission of full and short papers, representing original research, preliminary research results, proposals for new work, and position and opinion papers. All submitted papers will be peer-reviewed through double-blind reviewing process.Accepted papers will be published in the workshop proceedings, and will have to be presented at the workshop either as an oral presentation or as a poster. At least one author of each accepted paper is expected to register and attend the workshop to present the paper.All submissions must be written in English following the LNCS author guidelines. Full papers must not exceed 12 pages and short papers must not exceed 6 pages, including figures and references. Papers should be submitted as PDF files electronically through EasyChair.Important Dates- Full and short papers submission: 15 January 2018 (midnight AoE)- Notification of acceptance: 15 February 2018- Camera ready submission: 26 February 2018 (midnight AoE)- DroDyn Workshop: 26 March 2018- ECIR Conference: 26-29 March 2018Organizing Committee- Tamer Elsayed, Qatar University, Qatar- Walid Magdy, University of Edinburgh, UK- Mucahid Kutlu, Qatar University, Qatar- Maram Hasanain, Qatar University, Qatar- Reem Suwaileh, Qatar University, QatarFor any inquiries, contact us: telsayed@qu.edu.qa, wmagdy@inf.ed.ac.uk

postings.conferenceName: BUDAPEST 7th International Conference on “Bioscience, Chemical & Environmental Engineering” (BCE2-27) scheduled on April 28-30, 2027 Budapest (Hungary)
postings.conferenceText: Call for papers/TopicsAll Abstracts, Reviews, short articles, Full articles, Posters are welcomed related with any of the following research fields:Part 1: Independent Core TopicsThese topics represent the foundational knowledge and distinct pillars specific to each individual discipline.I. Bioscience Foundations Molecular and Cell Biology: Cellular structure, membrane transport, signal transduction, cell cycle regulation, and programmed cell death (apoptosis). Genetics and Genomics: Mendelian inheritance, molecular genetics (replication, transcription, translation), gene expression regulation, and epigenetics. Microbiology and Virology: Microbial structure, physiology, metabolic pathways of bacteria and fungi, viral replication cycles, and microbial pathogenesis. Organismal Anatomy and Physiology: Animal and plant physiology, homeostasis, immunology, and developmental biology. II. Chemical Engineering Foundations Transport Phenomena: Fluid mechanics (fluid flow, rheology), heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation), and mass transfer (diffusion, interphase mass transport). Chemical Thermodynamics: Classical laws of thermodynamics, phase equilibria, chemical reaction equilibria, and volumetric properties of pure fluids and mixtures. Reaction Engineering and Kinetics: Rate laws, ideal reactor design (Batch, CSTR, PFR), catalysis, heterogenous reaction kinetics, and reactor safety. Unit Operations and Separation Processes: Distillation, liquid-liquid extraction, gas absorption, drying, filtration, and crystallization. III. Environmental Engineering Foundations Hydrology and Water Resources Engineering: Surface water hydrology, groundwater flow, hydraulics of water distribution systems, and stormwater management. Atmospheric Science and Air Quality: Atmospheric chemistry, meteorology basics, air pollutant dispersion modeling, and ambient air quality standards. Solid and Hazardous Waste Management: Waste characterization, landfill design, hazardous waste identification, and radioactive waste management. Soil Mechanics and Geoenvironmental Engineering: Soil physics and chemistry, contaminant transport in porous media, and subsurface remediation techniques. Part 2: Interrelated & Convergent TopicsThese fields represent the massive overlap where Bioscience, Chemical Engineering, and Environmental Engineering merge to create advanced technologies and sustainable systems.I. Biochemical and Bioprocess Engineering(Intersection of Bioscience & Chemical Engineering) Enzyme Kinetics and Biocatalysis: Michaelis-Menten kinetics, enzyme immobilization techniques, and industrial enzyme applications. Bioreactor Design and Scale-Up: Fermenter design, aeration and agitation dynamics, sterilization kinetics, and continuous versus fed-batch cultivation. Downstream Processing: Separation and purification of biomolecules, cell disruption, chromatography, ultrafiltration, and lyophilization. Metabolic Engineering: Modification of metabolic pathways to optimize cellular production of chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and biofuels. II. Environmental Biotechnology(Intersection of Bioscience & Environmental Engineering) Biological Wastewater Treatment: Activated sludge processes, anaerobic digestion, trickling filters, and biological nutrient removal (nitrogen and phosphorus). Bioremediation and Phytoremediation: Microbial degradation of toxic hydrocarbons, heavy metal bioaccumulation, and the use of genetically engineered microbes for spill cleanup. Biofilms and Microbial Ecology: Formation, structure, and control of biofilms in engineering systems, and metagenomic analysis of engineered ecosystems. Biosensors for Environmental Monitoring: Development of cell-based and enzyme-based sensors for real-time detection of toxins, heavy metals, and pathogens. III. Sustainable Process Engineering & Green Chemistry(Intersection of Chemical Engineering & Environmental Engineering) Industrial Pollution Control: Design of air pollution control devices (scrubbers, electrostatic precipitators, cyclones) and industrial wastewater treatment networks. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA): Cradle-to-grave environmental impact evaluation of chemical products, carbon footprinting, and eco-efficiency metrics. Green Chemical Synthesis: Atom economy, replacement of hazardous solvents with supercritical fluids or ionic liquids, and energy-efficient chemical routes. Circular Economy and Waste Valorization: Conversion of plastic waste into chemical feedstocks (pyrolysis) and transforming agricultural residues into value-added materials. IV. The Grand Convergence: Bio-Environmental Chemical Systems(Intersection of All Three Disciplines) Biofuels and Renewable Energy Infrastructure: Thermochemical and biochemical conversion of biomass to bioethanol, biodiesel, biogas, and green hydrogen. Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS): Engineered chemical absorption systems combined with biological carbon fixation (e.g., microalgae photobioreactors). Synthetic Biology for Global Sustainability: Engineering synthetic consortia of microorganisms to simultaneously degrade plastics and synthesize biodegradable alternatives (PHA/PHB). Biomaterials and Tissue Engineering: Developing biocompatible polymers, scaffolds, and artificial organs using chemical process control and cellular biology principles.

postings.conferenceName: 59th ISTANBUL International Congress on Chemical, Biological & Environmental Engineering (ICBEE-26)
postings.conferenceText: Call for papers/TopicsFull Articles/ Reviews/ Shorts Papers/ Abstracts are welcomed in the following research fields:1. Chemical Engineering These topics form the bedrock of the discipline, focusing on how matter and energy are manipulated on a large scale. Transport Phenomena: The study of momentum (fluid mechanics), heat, and mass transfer. Chemical Thermodynamics: Phase equilibria, chemical reaction equilibria, and the laws governing energy conversion. Reaction Engineering & Kinetics: Design and optimization of chemical reactors ($r = kC^n$) and understanding the rates of chemical reactions. Separation Processes: Techniques to purify substances, including distillation, absorption, extraction, and membrane filtration. Process Control & Dynamics: Using mathematical models and sensors to maintain stability and safety in automated industrial systems. 2. Biological & Bioprocess EngineeringThis area applies engineering principles to biological systems, bridging the gap between "lab bench" biology and industrial production. Biochemical Engineering: Scaling up biological processes, such as fermentation for pharmaceuticals or biofuels. Cellular & Molecular Engineering: Manipulation of cell pathways and genetic engineering to produce specific proteins or metabolites. Biocatalysis: Using enzymes as industrial catalysts to perform highly specific chemical transformations. Synthetic Biology: Designing and constructing new biological parts, devices, and systems for practical purposes. Bioinformatics: Using computational tools to analyze large biological datasets, such as genomic sequences. 3. Environmental Engineering & SustainabilityThis branch focuses on protecting human health and the environment by managing waste and resources. Water & Wastewater Treatment: Physical, chemical, and biological methods to purify water for consumption or safe discharge. Air Quality Engineering: Control of particulate matter and gaseous pollutants (like $SO_x$ and $NO_x$) from industrial sources. Solid & Hazardous Waste Management: The treatment, disposal, and recycling of industrial and municipal waste. Environmental Remediation: Cleanup of contaminated soil and groundwater using techniques like bioremediation or soil vapor extraction. Sustainability & Life Cycle Assessment (LCA): Quantifying the total environmental impact of a product from "cradle to grave." 4. Interrelated & Emerging Cross-Disciplinary TopicsThese subtopics represent the areas where the three main branches overlap significantly. Green Chemistry & Engineering: Designing chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use and generation of hazardous substances. Biorefinery Systems: Integrating chemical and biological processes to convert biomass into fuels, power, and chemicals (a bridge between all three fields). Waste-to-Energy (WtE): Using chemical or biological methods (like anaerobic digestion or gasification) to turn waste streams into energy. Nanotechnology: Engineering materials at the molecular scale for targeted drug delivery (Bio/Chem) or high-efficiency water filters (Env/Chem). Sustainable Energy Systems: Development of fuel cells, solar cells, and advanced batteries using chemical and material science principles. Systems Biology & Ecology: Using mathematical modeling to understand complex interactions within a biological cell or an entire ecosystem.
